scope: Read-only native scripts and existing generated engine documentation; no game launch, GUI, production changes, tool changes, or acceptance run.

lines.text: # I then find the scrap_miner job (in pop_jobs) and change its category from planet_miners to planet_scrap_miners.
# Since planet_scrap_miners is a child of planet_miners, Scrap Miners will now receive the effects of both
# IMPORTANT!  _add modifiers don't apply to children categories, only _mult ones do. This is working as intended.
# Limiting _add inheritance is necessary to avoid unintentional cascade effects.
# IMPORTANT!  An _add modifier is applied once per resource table filed under its category on the same object.
# Most objects declare their category once, so this makes no difference. A pop group is the exception. It holds one
# resource table from its species archetype, and one more from each trait, and once all of them used planet_pops. An _add
# modifier on planet_pops was applied once for each of those tables, and the total changes with the trait list of the
# species. Put such a modifier on a category that only one resource table uses. The archetype tables stay on planet_pops
# for this reason, and the trait tables use the hidden child category planet_pops_traits.
# You can also define triggered modifiers, which will apply in the same way as mult and add modifiers normally do, but with the extra condition that a trigger must return true.
# The format for these is triggered_produces_modifier, etc (see below)
# These are useful if e.g. you want to apply an effect only to biological pops. Note however that if you do something too complicated in these, and then use the modifiers in a lot
# of places, then it can have a bit of a performance impact (it will check these triggers whenever it is working out what resources a resource table contains, and there is a non-zero
# value for this triggered modifier. So not the worst, but don't go crazy!).

round_to = 0.01 #DO NOT REMOVE. It is here to stop modifiers perpetually being recalculated because complex dependency

resource = { minerals = 0.5 energy = 0.5 } (for evaluating the bonuses to multiple resources, with weights)
species_modifiers_only = no (default: yes - only checks trait modifiers, trait triggered pop modifiers, and species habitability)
Supported Scopes: planet ship pop_group colony

time_multiplier = <variable> (optional: days/months/years value is multiplied by the value of this variable)
clear_on_owner_change = yes (optional: default no; clears modifier if planet/system/megastructure's owner changes)
Supported Scopes: megastructure planet country ship pop pop_group fleet galactic_object pop_faction federation starbase spy_network espionage_operation astral_rift cosmic_storm_influence_field colony
resource_income_compare - Checks specific resource income value for the country scope (note: checks profit minus loss, not revenue):

category = <category_name> # Optional; if not provided, will use sum for all Categories

export_resource_income_to_variable - Exports the value of the current country's monthly income of the specified resource to a variable.

steal_planet_output - Steals resource output from a planet and gives it to a target empire or stockpile.

resource groups: basic, advanced, strategic, rare, other, research, material (material = basic + advanced + strategic + rare)
DEFAULT_CHANGE_JOB_THRESHOLD		= 1.05		# A job must have this much higher weight in order for a pop to switch to it from their current job

POP_JOB_WORKFORCE_WEIGHT_POWER		= 3			# Workforce factor is raised to this power when calculating job weights, amplifying differences between pops. 1 = linear, 3 = industrious (+0.15) miner gets 1.15^3 = 1.52x weight.
FAVORITE_JOB_WEIGHT_MULT			= 10.0		# Weight multiplier applied to a job marked as the planet favorite, ensuring it fills before other jobs of the same stratum rank.
MIN_MODIFIER_MULT 					= -0.9		# Used for various modifer multipliers to cap the multiplication from reaching 0 or negative values.
MIN_ECONOMIC_MODIFIER_MULT 			= -0.9		# Cost, upkeep and production modifiers generated through the economic system (common/economic_categories) cannot go beyond this point
# Explicit rc fallback: additive native job-output modifier, not a final-output multiplier.

native_jobs_inventory.method: Top-level block definitions in common/pop_jobs/*.txt with category, resources or is_capped_by_modifier; includes swapped and fake definitions; does not assert all are enabled resource jobs. output/ references counted syntactically, not recursively expanded.

limited_modifier_interface_search.interpretation: Zero matches under these explicit name patterns is not a proof that the engine has no multiplicative arithmetic or future extension. Existing native produces.mult and output reader are positive capabilities.

points: A pop group can supply multiple jobs.
Bonus workforce is separate from production bonuses and scales job upkeep as well as output.
Pop upkeep and job upkeep are distinct.
official_primary_context.version_limit: Historical 4.0 design diary, corroborates architecture and a material maintenance risk; not a new 4.5.2 runtime probe.

conclusion: Under current nationwide-job, maintenance-unchanged, no blanket vanilla/third-party job overrides and no monthly subsidy constraints, no sufficiently established suitable final independent channel was found. Preserve user-authorized additive fallback; do not claim a universal mathematical impossibility.
